meta.name: Bellrock Coast
meta.note: Generated by tools/genworld.mjs; safe to hand-edit.

hello.text: Kelp. I stretch new rope between the road posts until it forgets how to kink. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: Step over the line, not on it.

hello.text: Chalk. I mark boats, walls, and anything else expected to be found in fog. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: White first. Color after the weather agrees.

hello.text: Morrow. I cast small bells for doors too far inland to hear the rock. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: A clear note needs room around it.

text: Tide is doing what it likes today. It usually is.
Doss. Off the boats, mostly. You will have come down the road -- everyone comes down the road.

third.text: Back down. It is the better end of the town, this.

text: Sheep, and Nell, and more of the same for as far as you would care to walk.
It does not stop. That is the difference between here and an island, and it is the whole difference.

sea.text: Weather, mostly. And the bell rock, which you will hear before you ever see it.

trade.text: Three good ones. The shop will not pay you that, whatever they tell you.

after.text: Tide still doing what it likes.

bye.text: Mind the weed on the slip.

text: You climbed all four steps. Most stop at two and say they have seen it.
Nell. Top field is mine. From here the sea is a thing that happens down there.

again.text: Up again. The wind is worse and the view is better.

gift.text: In the sheep-cropped bits, where the grass is short enough to see them. Take these.

text: North? Nobody has ever come back and told me it stopped.
That is why I am up here and Doss is down there. Neither of us is right.
Halfway up and halfway down. Best row in the town and nobody agrees.
Sennen. Door is open to you now -- kettle is usually on and the fire usually is not.
House is two houses, mind. Boards up the hill side, flags down the sea side, and a step between them.

welcome.text: Come in whenever. You know where it is. Both ways round, remember.

text: That was you on the bell.
Whole coast heard it and every one of them thought it was for them. That is the trick of the thing.

choices.text: Why is there a bell in your front room?
Why two ramps and not one?
Does anybody agree with you about anything?

both.text: Both, obviously. That is what a coast is and they both think it is a betrayal.

trade.text: For the window. It faces the road and the road deserves better. Here.

text: Because this house is the only one both halves can hear at the same time. Somebody had to have it.
Sea gets the note first and the hill sends it back about a second later. I timed it with a candle.
Ring it if you are in there. Everybody stops. It is the best second of anybody's day.
Because with one you go up and come back down the same way, and that is a corridor, not a house.
With two you can go round. Same as the town. I did not build the town but I did build the ramps.
Nell says the sea is a thing that happens down there. Doss says the hill is somewhere you go when the tide is wrong.
They are both describing my front room and neither of them will come and stand in it.

hello.text: Ballast. Rope Walker for the harbor. The bell rings true and so do I. That's my door by the coil of rope.

again.text: The tide table's never wrong. The tide, occasionally.

hello.text: Fresh off the road, are you? Buoy, Bell Ringer. Bellrock keeps time by the bell and the tide, in that order.

again.text: Ships come back. That's the whole trick of a harbor.

hello.text: Capstan. I serve as Chart Mender. Every rope in this town has a job, and so does everyone holding one.

again.text: Polish the brass and the weather behaves. Proven fact.

hello.text: Mind the wet stones on the quay. Chandler -- Harbor Reckoner. Come by when the fog horn's quiet.

again.text: The bell's a half-tone flat in cold weather. Charming, really.

hello.text: Cleat, Signal Keeper. A harbor is a promise the town makes to boats.

again.text: Fog's due. I can smell it thinking.

hello.text: Aye, hello. Davit. Been Anchor Smith since the old bell cracked and got recast. It sounds better with the scar.

again.text: A coiled rope is a happy rope.
